subject: Dressing-room storage that feels calm
hook: A calm dressing room is planned, not tidied.
ig:
A calm dressing room is planned, not tidied. Five layout rules worth knowing before anyone draws a thing.

Most dressing rooms feel cluttered for the same reason: everything is visible, in three different finishes, with nowhere fixed to go.

1. Close the doors on the busy stuff. Folded knitwear, bags and gym kit look messy on open shelves no matter how neat you are.
2. Pick one finish and run it everywhere. Matt white or oak-effect across carcasses, doors and shelves reads as one quiet wall.
3. Drawers at hand height, long hanging at the end. Hems stop crowding the middle of the run.
4. Give every item an address. Drawer dividers, a shoe pull-out, a tray for watches.
5. Plan to about 80% full. Spare space is what keeps it calm a year from now.

This is the kind of thing we work through at a free, no-obligation design consultation before we measure up for fitted wardrobes or a walk-in.
